page.layout: Two oval portrait medallions side by side at the top, centred, each with its legend around the rim (left: TVRC. MOSE.; right: TVRC. IMP. MAHOMETES). Below them one column of running text in two paragraphs. The signature "Nnn" stands at the foot right of the text. A printed ornament lies below, without text. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: MOSES Orchanem nepotem,cui erat patruus interfecit, ipse quoque à fratre Mahometo vicissim interfectus est. nec connumeratur ambo in serie Turcicorum Imperatorum, quòd paucis admodum diebus imperitarint. Vide Richerium de rebus Turcicis lib.i.

MAHOMETES huius nominis primus, Mustaphæ & Mosis,eius inquam qui Orchanem ex fratre nepotem è medio fustulerat,frater, post Baiazetem Turcis imperat anno mundi 5359. à Christo nato 1397. Sunt qui ea quæ de Cyriscelebe feruntur,huic vni tribuant. Is itaque Bulgaros & Valachos præ dis & cladibus afflixit, tributúmque magnum impofuit. Arma deinde in Satrapas Asiæ vertit, loca omnia quæ Tamberlanes occupauerat recepit : nihil generis propinquitate commotus, Turcicæ nationis complures principes ex Galatia, Ponto & Cappadocia pulsos extirpauit : alios autem integros atque incolumes seruauit. Reuersus in Græciam, Adrianopolim, quæ caput est Thraciæ, sedis imperatoriæ loco habuit, pulsis illinc Christianis. Obiit anno imperij sui 17. regni verò Caroli hoc nomine sexti Francorum Regis 35. Vide Richer.lib.i. & Cosm. Munst.lib.4.

page.notes: The two medallion legends are printed around the portrait rims and are given above as running lines. Doubtful readings: "lib.i." (the numeral may be a small r or i), and "Cyriscelebe" (the printed form is close to Cyri1celebe, with the l hard to separate). The medallion portraits carry no further text. The faint show-through lines below the text are not transcribed.
